data.title: Digital vassals? French Government ‘exposes citizens’ data to US'
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 法国参议院在一份报告中批评政府及公共部门过度依赖美国科技巨头，如微软，称此举威胁国家数字主权，可能导致“主权自杀”。报告指出，法国将关键数据基础设施外包给受美国域外法律管辖的公司，使公共数据暴露于美国监控之下，特别是根据《外国情报监视法》（FISA）和《澄清合法海外数据使用法》（CLOUD）。微软法务总监承认无法保证法国数据不会被交给外国当局。参议院还指责政府贬低欧洲替代方案，过于关注价格而忽视法律和战略风险。与此同时，其他欧洲国家如丹麦已开始减少对美国科技公司的依赖。法国议员呼吁欧盟暂停与美国的隐私保护协议，以应对主权风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲在数据主权、IT基础设施选择以及对美国科技巨头的依赖方面的讨论和争议

不同观点：
• Saline9515认为，法国政府选择微软产品并非出于成本或效率考虑，而是因为政府人员对微软的依赖以及不愿学习新工具。他还分享了个人经历，表明在试图转向开源软件R或Python时遇到了内部抵制。
• mananaysiempre关注数据收集量的问题，认为减少数据收集是关键，因为即使数据在一个司法管辖区内，也可能成为攻击目标。
• afarah1引用了CJEU的裁决，指出美国在隐私问题上的立场与欧盟法律不兼容，并对欧盟委员会一再认可与美国的协议表示质疑。
• ColinWright分享了一段法国参议院的会议记录，显示微软法国代表无法保证法国公民的数据不会被美国政府传唤。
• crop_rotation批评欧盟没有建立本土软件生态系统，并指出中国在这方面的优势。
• phtrivier指出法国和欧盟内部开始出现对数据主权和减少对美国依赖的讨论，但实际进展缓慢。
• isodev建议对涉及美国科技公司的产品应有更透明的披露和警告。
• CalRobert提到欧洲对微软Azure的依赖令人费解。
• reestr认为，数据基础设施的控制权比平台的所有权更重要，一旦暴露结构中，主权就成为一种错觉。
• hollowonepl质疑美国设备与中国的设备在监听方面是否有本质区别。
• SpicyLemonZest指出，数字主权需要强大的本土软件产业支持，并提到欧洲解决方案常被误认为成本过高或效率低下。
• MEMORYC_RRUPTED分享了比利时和荷兰的情况，指出政府部门对微软系统的依赖以及转型困难。
• stef25对讨论的网站提出质疑，认为其有亲俄罗斯倾向，并提供了相关背景资料。
• bpavuk提到法国尝试通过Mistral和La Suite来引领数据主权，但对其实施情况表示疑惑。
• rdm_blackhole总结了从美国科技巨头转型的困难，指出无论是转向开源软件还是开发本土解决方案，都需要大量时间和成本，而欧盟在这方面已经落后。

补充讨论：
• 数据主权和隐私保护的争议焦点在于欧盟与美国之间的法律和协议不兼容性，以及美国政府可能通过法律手段获取欧盟公民数据。
• 欧洲在建立自主IT基础设施和软件生态系统方面面临巨大挑战，包括技术转型难度、成本问题以及政治和经济利益的牵扯。
• 对数据收集和监控的广泛关注，反映了公众和政府在数字化时代对隐私和安全的日益重视。
• 对讨论平台和信息来源的质疑反映了信息可信度和潜在政治倾向在公共讨论中的重要性。

The French Senate slams the French governement and public services deepening reliance on American tech giants, warning of a looming “sovereignty suicide". Getty
News
16 July 2025
Digital vassals? French Government ‘exposes citizens’ data to US’
Anne-Laure Dufeal
Share
France’s deepening reliance on US tech giants is raising alarms about digital sovereignty and exposing public data to foreign jurisdictions.
In a French Senate report on economic and digital sovereignty, Senators accused the French State of “political fault”. That was in regard to outsourcing essential data infrastructure to US companies subject to US extraterritorial laws, including
Microsoft
, despite repeated warnings and alternatives.
“France is subject to US extraterritorial law,” the report stated, warning that public data, including from health, education and critical sectors, was exposed to foreign surveillance under US legislation such as the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) and the Clarifying Lawful Overseas Use of Data Act (CLOUD).
This legislation allowed the US Government to demand that companies subject to US law disclose the data they stored, simply by obtaining a judge’s authorisation.
The Senate report cited Microsoft France’s legal director, Anton Carniaux, as admitting the company could not guarantee that French data it hosted would not be handed over to foreign authorities.
“Carniaux … was asked by the [French Senate] commission to guarantee that French citizens’ data hosted by Microsoft would never be transmitted to foreign authorities without the agreement of the French authorities. He replied: ‘No, I can’t guarantee that,'” the report stated.
US tech giant Microsoft presented new plans promising to improve the European cloud customers’ data protection.
https://t.co/lkX1ysk1vy
— Brussels Signal (@brusselssignal)
June 18, 2025
In March 2025, the Ministry of Education signed a €74 million deal with a US company for equipping its departments and universities.
The country’s elite school for engineers, École Polytechnique, also decided earlier this year to move the school’s IT system to Microsoft.
That was done despite earlier instructions from the French Government urging school districts to avoid deploying Microsoft or Google collaborative tools due to sovereignty risks.
The CNLL (National Council for Free Software) warned that “legal, technical, and strategic risks are being deliberately ignored.”
Speaking with
Brussels Signal
on July 16, French MP Philippe Latombe blames France’s “bureaucratic inertia”.
“There is no real connection between political leaders and French civil servants, who think they will remain in their posts indefinitely. This creates bureaucratic inertia. They secured early contracts easily because they have always been there, which leads to habitual reliance by public buyers,” he said.
In their report, the French Senate accused the government of systematically discrediting European alternatives, claiming they were “too costly” or “not efficient enough”.
“The commission of inquiry found that European solutions were systematically denigrated by the government, wrongly judged to be too costly or inefficient,” the report read.
For Latombe, France needs to move beyond price, and consider other factors like the fact that French companies contribute to the national social system, such as social security contributions, taxes.
French MP Philippe Latombe has urged European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to suspend the US-EU Data Privacy Framework before President-elect Donald Trump assumes office.
https://t.co/ni5C4rYxxW
— Brussels Signal (@brusselssignal)
November 15, 2024
In November last year,
Latombe criticised
the US-EU Data Privacy Framework (DPF) deal, saying it no longer served EU interests due to the US president’s “impulsive” nature.
The DPF was designed to make it easier for companies to transfer personal data such as names, addresses and browsing history from the EU to the US.
Another striking example comes from the cybersecurity sector.
In early 2025, the French cybersecurity firm VADE merged with Germany’s Hornet Security, forming what appeared to be a promising EU-based leader in international cloud security. However, just a year later, in March 2025, US company Proofpoint acquired the entire Hornetsecurity Group.
“As a result, there is no longer a fully French solution in this strategic sector”, denounced Latombe.
Tech giant Meta has snubbed a ‘cease and desist’ request from the European digital rights watchdog over their use of personal data to train AI systems.
https://t.co/tvtJr51KkD
— Brussels Signal (@brusselssignal)
May 15, 2025
While France deepened its digital dependency, other European nations have been pushing back.
In June 2025, Denmark’s Minister for Digitalisation, Caroline Stage Olsen, announced a full pivot away from Microsoft, replacing it with LibreOffice, a Berlin-based open-source alternative.

data.title: Java was not underhyped in 1997 (2021)
data.author: SerCe
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Java在1997年时的巨大影响力以及其后来为何失去关注。作者Dylan Beattie回忆了1997年他在大学学习计算机科学时，Java是必修课，并且被广泛应用于各种课程中。Java在当时因其自动垃圾回收、并发处理、异常处理等创新特性备受推崇，甚至被认为能解决所有问题，取代桌面应用和微软Windows系统。Corel等公司曾计划将重要软件移植到Java平台，Java applets被视为网络应用的未来。然而，Java的实际表现不如预期，在桌面应用和游戏开发方面不如Visual Basic、C++，而在服务器端网络编程方面则面临Perl、PHP等竞争。Java虽好，但并未能如 hype 所预期的那样彻底改变计算机世界。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Java的“ hype”（炒作）历史及其技术能力与市场影响

不同观点：
• **Java技术能力的“未被充分炒作”**：
  - **jasode**指出，Java在技术特性上（如类型系统和包管理器）具备优势，但这些优势未被充分认识和利用，因此在技术圈中是“未被充分炒作”的。
  - 例子：Java的强类型系统有助于防止错误，但未像JavaScript或Python那样广泛使用。

• **Java市场效应的“过度炒作”**：
  - **jasode**也提到，Java在1990年代被过度炒作，尤其是其对整个计算领域的影响，如“Write Once, Run Anywhere”的承诺没有实现。
  - 例子：Java未能取代微软的Windows，也未能在桌面应用和网页插件方面取得成功。

• **Java的企业适用性和成本效益**：
  - **bane**认为Java在企业环境中取得成功，因其帮助公司降低了开发成本并提高了可靠性，特别是通过减少内存管理等复杂问题。
  - Java被用于自动化业务流程，尽管其对高技能开发者的需求较低。

• **Java在教育和市场推广中的策略**：
  - **vanschelven**提到Sun公司通过学术策略和品牌推广，使Java在大学教育中广泛传播。
  - **jerf**补充，Java在1997年的硬件条件下无法实现其被炒作的承诺，且通过大量广告和付费推广进入学校和企业。

  - **rr808**认为Java和JVM本身很好，但企业开发中常用的Spring框架过于复杂，难以理解。

• **Java的长期稳健性和实用性**：
  - **lordleft**指出Java仍然是许多大公司（如Google和Amazon）的选择，证明了其稳健性和实用性。

• **对当前技术炒作的反思**：
  - **stephenlf**将1990年代的Java炒作与当前的生成式AI炒作进行比较，暗示历史可能重演。

• **Java的技术局限和替代方案**：
  - **liampulles**分享了自己从Java开发转向其他技术的经历，认为Java容易导致复杂架构。
  - **binarymax**批评Java缺乏对无符号数值的原生支持。

• **Java的历史贡献和影响**：
  - **jmyeet**详细回顾了Java在1990年代的三个主要炒作方向（桌面应用、服务器应用和浏览器应用），并认为Java在服务器领域取得了持久成功，且对互联网的民主化有重要贡献。

• **Java与其他技术的市场竞争**：
  - **w10-1**分析了Java在不同公司和平台之间的市场竞争，包括VM许可证、IDE市场以及企业级Java许可。
  - 提到IBM、Oracle、Microsoft等公司在Java生态系统中的角色和策略。

• **对“炒作”一词的批评**：
  - **vardump**认为“炒作”一词常被无理由地用来攻击新生和流行的事物。

• Java在1990年代是否被过度炒作及其在现代技术环境中的地位和实用性。

44590034.article_content:
Java Criminally Underhyped? Not Back in 1997.
Posted by
Dylan Beattie
on
01 July 2021
•
permalink
Earlier today, a fun little moment of
Twitter serendipity
alerted me to an article by Jackson Roberts, a computer science student at the University of Colorado, entitled “
Java is criminally underhyped
”. It’s a really interesting article, and Jackson’s observations correlate with a lot of my own thinking about languages and platforms, although I am squarely in the .NET / CLR camp on that particular front.
But Jackson ends his article:
I am curious why Java lost its hype in the first place. Programmer culture history is poorly documented and if you have insight, please
email me
or leave a comment.
And, well, the comment I was leaving got a bit long, so I figured I’d blog about it instead. You see, I studied computer science at the University of Southampton, from 1997 to 2000, and when I was an undergraduate, the hype about Java was unbelievable. Java was too important to ignore; it was released in January 1996, and by the time I started university in September 1997 it was a mandatory course for all first year students; it was used throughout my degree course, right up to the final year module on programming language design where our coursework assignment was to build a Scheme interpreter – in Java.
Java circa 1997 was probably the most hyped thing I have ever seen in my career.
For starters, it was the first really mainstream language to introduce a lot of features we now take for granted in most high-level languages. Memory management? Readers, even to a first-year comp sci undergraduate who had spent a grand total of six weeks working with
malloc
and
free
, Java’s automatic garbage collection was clearly a revelation. Concurrency? It has threads. They work. Job done. Exceptions? You mean I can just write functions that return what I want, instead of functions that leave the result in a
char*
pointer somewhere and return an arbitrary non-zero integer if it worked? Java introduced a lot of incredibly powerful ideas and patterns, and it’s hard to underestimate how much impact it would have on the next two decades of programming language design.
But Java wasn’t content with that. Java was going to solve ALL the problems. JavaScript? The language that would end up taking over the world wide web? JavaScript was a glue language. The idea was that all your
serious
applications would be deployed as Java applets, with JavaScript used for only the most superficial wiring between applets. Java applets were such a big deal in 1997 that some people seriously believed that they represented the end of desktop applications, the end of Microsoft Windows; even the end of the computer as we knew it.
Corel, who at the time were still a credible threat to Microsoft’s emerging monopoly, announced in 1996 that they were porting their WordPerfect office suite and their market-leading CorelDRAW! graphics software to Java. Check out
this Infoworld article from 1996
to see just how deep the hype hole really went:
“The success of Java-based network computers, and perhaps Java itself, will likely require the availability of vertical productivity applications for word processing, spreadsheets and databases. At the JavaOne conference, Corel Corp. (www.corel.com) made a first stab at offering such products with the announcement that it plans to deliver a suite of office applications based on its QuattroPro and WordPerfect products. Both products should be available for sale by early next year.”
Java was going to revolutionise desktop development: Java Swing and the Java Native Interface (JNI) meant you could write your app once, and run it on Windows, Linux and Solaris.
1
And thanks to the amazing power of JavaBeans, once you had implemented a particular service or algorithm, you could create a “bean” for it and it could be reused anywhere, by anybody, and building software would be as easy as putting together Lego bricks. JavaBeans were often cited as the last component model we would ever need.
There was an industry spec for a “
Network Computer
”, a device profile that mandated support for HTTP, Java, JPEG and a handful of other standards… hardware companies would build and sell Network Computers, developers would use Java’s “write once, run anywhere” model to build software for Network Computers, and the entire future would be Java applets running on set-top boxes (or “net-top boxes” as they were often dubbed.) Sun Microsystems actually shipped a thing called the JavaStation, a device based on their SPARCstation platform that ran JavaOS.
The problem is: Java was good, but it wasn’t
that
good. For Windows desktop apps, Visual Basic and Visual C++ could run rings around it. For games and anything where performance was a consideration, C++ all the way, especially as we entered an age of affordable 3D graphics cards and OpenGL became a big deal. And for server-side web programming, we had Perl, PHP, Microsoft Active Server Pages, and good ol

data.title: Dual interfacial H-bonding-enhanced deep-blue hybrid copper–iodide LEDs
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种基于无毒铜碘杂化物的高效深蓝光LED。该材料具有接近 unity 的光致发光量子产率（99.4 ± 0.4%），发射波长为449 nm，色坐标为(0.147, 0.087)。通过使用这种杂化铜碘化合物作为唯一的发光层，并采用双界面氢键钝化策略，显著提升了LED的性能。该策略有效优化了电荷注入，实现了12.57%的最大外量子效率和3970.30 cd m^-2的最大亮度，色坐标为(0.147, 0.091)。此外，器件在环境条件下具有204小时的工作稳定性，并展示了4 cm^2大面积器件的高效性。研究表明，铜碘基杂化材料在固态照明和显示技术中具有广阔应用前景。

Abstract
Solution-processed light-emitting diodes based on non-toxic copper–iodide hybrids are a compelling solution for efficient and stable deep-blue lighting, attributed to their tunability, high photoluminescence efficiency, and environmental sustainability. Here we present a new hybrid copper iodide that exhibits near-unity photoluminescence quantum yield (99.4 ± 0.4%) with an emission wavelength of 449 nm and color coordinates (0.147, 0.087), alongside its emission mechanism and charge transport characteristics. We use the thin film of this hybrid as the sole active emissive layer (EML) to fabricate deep-blue LEDs and subsequently enhance the device performance via a unique dual interfacial hydrogen bond passivation strategy. This synergetic surface modification approach, integrating a new H-bond donor self-assembled monolayer with an ultra-thin PMMA capping layer, effectively passivates both heterojunctions of the copper–iodide hybrid EML and optimizes charge injections. We achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 12.57%, maximum luminance of 3970.30 cd m
−2
with color coordinates (0.147, 0.091), and an excellent operational stability (
T
50
) of 204 hours under ambient conditions. We further showcase a large-area device of 4 cm
2
that maintains high efficiency. Our findings reveal the potential of copper iodide-based hybrid materials for applications in solid-state lighting and display technologies, offering a versatile strategy for enhancing device performances.

have gained recognition as promising candidates. They have been utilized as emitting layers via solution processing and achieved impressive performance in green and lower energy LEDs. However, developing efficient blue, and particularly deep-blue, LEDs that align with the Rec. 2020 primary blue for full-color displays poses a significant challenge for these materials
7
. Conventional blue organic LEDs (OLEDs) and perovskite LEDs (PeLEDs) demonstrate compromised structural and spectral stability under elevated operational biases

. Additionally, lead-based perovskites

and Cd-based quantum dots

are subject to concerns over environmental issues due to their toxicity, while the deployment of low-toxic phosphorescence organic emitters

, InP- and ZnSe-based QDs

is constrained by their high cost in complex design and synthetic process. These challenges limit the practical application of these materials and raise difficulties to cover the full color gamut. Consequently, developing cost-effective, eco-friendly, and efficient emitters for solution-processed deep-blue LEDs is vital for the advancement of comprehensive SSL and display technologies.

data.title: How Tesla is proving doubters right on why its robotaxi service cannot scale
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 特斯拉在奥斯汀推出的机器人出租车服务因一次险些致命的事故显示出其技术仍不成熟，当时车辆试图非法穿越铁路，而火车即将驶来，安全员不得不介入控制。尽管特斯拉的完全自动驾驶（FSD）技术已有进步，但数据显示每340英里仍会出现关键故障，如闯红灯或逆行。专家认为，特斯拉过于急于推出服务，以转移投资者对其销售下滑和电动卡车项目失败的关注。当前技术远未达到安全扩展服务的要求，每次增加车辆都会增加事故风险。特斯拉CEO马斯克正押注于这一变革性技术，但其可靠性仍存疑。

主要讨论点：特斯拉的机器人出租车（Robotaxi）项目的可行性、安全性、及其与现有公共交通系统的比较。

不同观点：
• **质疑机器人出租车的规模化和实用性**：[general1726] 认为特斯拉的机器人出租车无法在城市中有效扩展，因为城市交通容量有限，将单人乘坐的汽车放入城市会造成交通拥堵。他建议使用如公交车、地铁等已有的大容量交通工具，并指出这些交通工具的发展是自然的演变结果，而特斯拉没有理解这一点。

• **质疑商业模式的可行性**：[moogly] 认为特斯拉作为一个前瞻性的汽车制造商，运营低利润的出租车服务并不合理。他还对个人汽车加入车队盈利模式表示怀疑，指出车辆磨损、保险、清洁和充电等问题。此外，他质疑特斯拉如果认为机器人出租车盈利，为什么不自己运营车队而是卖车。

• **安全性和品牌声誉问题**：[breadwinner] 和 [findthewords] 都提到了特斯拉FSD（全自动驾驶）的事故记录，特别是与Waymo的对比，指出Waymo在安全性上表现更好。他们认为特斯拉在安全性上不如竞争对手，且对仅依靠视觉的自动驾驶技术持怀疑态度。

• **专业司机能力与AI对比**：[labrador] 强调机器人出租车应具备与专业司机相同的能力，认为目前的AI技术无法替代专业司机，特别是在处理复杂或极端情况时。

• **对特斯拉及其CEO的批评**：[codechicago277] 批评马斯克在扩展机器人出租车服务时的不严肃态度，认为这种行为不负责任且影响品牌信誉。

• **对数据透明性和责任的担忧**：[jqpabc123] 指出特斯拉在安全数据上的不透明性，并担心选择信任特斯拉技术的人可能将他人置于危险之中，特别是当机器人出租车发生事故时的责任归属问题。

• **对特斯拉未来成功的信心**：[DustinBrett] 和 [fossuser] 等人对特斯拉的技术和未来持乐观态度，认为批评者只是怀疑者，特斯拉有能力证明他们 wrong。

• **技术实现和成本优化讨论**：[maxlin] 和 [Closi] 讨论了特斯拉在技术实现上的优势，如不依赖高清地图和低成本传感器，使其具备可扩展性。但[Closi] 也指出特斯拉在技术实现上的约束可能影响其在“登月项目”中的成功。

补充讨论：
• **对具体事件和视频的讨论**：[ArtTimeInvestor] 和 [ChrisMarshallNY] 提到了一个YouTube视频和相关事件，认为这些事件被夸大以批评特斯拉的项目，但总体上项目进展良好。

争议焦点：
• 特斯拉机器人出租车的安全性、商业可行性以及与现有公共交通系统的比较是主要争议点。批评者认为特斯拉低估了城市交通的复杂性和安全性要求，而支持者则相信特斯拉的技术潜力和未来成功。

A near-deadly accident with a car driving towards an oncoming train show humans are still needed in Tesla robotaxis to prevent collisions.
(Allison Robbert—AFP via Getty Images)
Tesla
CEO Elon Musk launched his Austin robotaxi service nearly a month ago to great fanfare
. But FSD Community Tracker host Elias Martinez argues everything that has happened since explains why the service has not scaled—it remains nowhere near safe enough to remove human safety monitors, as proven by a near accident.
The very day Elon Musk expanded the boundaries of his three-week-old autonomous ride hailing service in Austin, Joe Tegtmeyer’s Tesla tried to illegally run a railroad crossing just as a locomotive approached.
“The robotaxi did not see that, and the safety observer had to stop the vehicle until the train had passed. So there’s a little bit of work that still needs to be polished up with the software, but otherwise it’s been just an amazing opportunity to see how well the expanded service is working,” he said on Monday in a
post on X
.
Taking what might have been a life-threatening situation seemingly in stride, Tegtmeyer then argued in favor of Tesla adding more cars to the 10 or so currently on the roads to cut waiting times that had ballooned to 20 minutes.
None of this comes as a surprise to Elias Martinez. One of the earliest Full Self-Driving beta testers, he says Tesla’s software has “come a long way” over the past four years. But he argues all available evidence points to the technology being nowhere near robust enough to support the 10,000 cars Musk
claimed in May
were possible in theory on day one.
“These issues prove Tesla should never have launched even with just 10 vehicles,” he tells
Fortune.
“Yes, it works most of the time, but it blows my mind we’re still seeing issues like FSD running red lights or driving on the wrong side of the road. This shouldn’t be happening on such a regular basis.”
The problem is with each car added, the greater the statistical chance of a collision. Any robotaxi service, Waymo included, needs to be virtually flawless in order to scale the service safely—yet with Tesla there’s no sign of that, according to Martinez.

ride complete! Follow along on this ride with me and I’ve got some observations and things to talk about along the way!
This ride was almost perfect but I did have one instance of the safety driver having to intervene at a rail road crossing, which I…
pic.twitter.com/CQwKuHU8Nx
— Joe Tegtmeyer 🚀 🤠🛸😎 (@JoeTegtmeyer)
July 14, 2025
A distraction from declining sales numbers
The former U.S. Marine hosts the crowd-sourced
FSD Community Tracker
, the single most sophisticated and reliable form of empirical data collection and analysis on Tesla’s self-driving technology that is publicly available. Car executives like
Volkswagen
Autonomous Mobility CEO
Christian Senger
speak highly of it as a benchmark, and even Musk—who has his own internal data on disengagements that he refuses to share—singled it out as proof the company is making progress.
Developed with the help of a Canadian Tesla driver, his tracker is simple and easy to use: during a trip, FSD beta testers like Martinez catalog in real time problems that arise directly into the vehicle’s onboard infotainment system, where it’s stored until it can be uploaded to the internet. Drivers are incentivized through weekly recognition of the top contributors, turning it into something of a friendly competition.
Currently,
its data shows
even the latest FSD version from Tesla results in a critical disengagement roughly every 340 miles between both city and highway at present. Called 13.2.9, it rolled out in May just weeks before the Austin service launched. “You sometimes hear Elon saying, ‘we’re having a hard time finding disengagements.’ That is
such
BS,” Martinez adds.
Although the Austin robotaxi fleet is believed to be using a newer iteration, in Martinez’s estimation it closely approximates the performance of the version released to the public since they reveal similar shortcomings, such as driving in the wrong lane.
He believes Tesla has been more focused on meeting Musk’s June launch timetable come hell or high water than on perfecting the actual underlying technology. Since demand for his EVs dropped sharply in the first half of the year and his Cybertruck has proven to be a commercial flop, the CEO needs something to keep investors happy.
“This feels like a distraction from the declining sales numbers,” he said, adding “Elon is gambling.”
In the meantime, the last major update Tesla owners received, v13.2.1, launched to the public
seven months ago
.
The company did not respond to a request to comment on this or any other point related to its FSD self-driving technology.

data.title: Scientists reveal a widespread but unidentified psychological phenomenon
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了一种称为“回避折返”的行为，即人们往往不愿意回头选择更高效的路径，即使这能节省时间和精力。这种行为不仅出现在实际的物理任务中，也存在于心理任务中。研究发现，这种现象并非由于对成本的错误估计，而是因为人们不愿意否定已经完成的努力。在一系列实验中，参与者在面对需要折返或重新开始的任务时，往往选择继续当前的低效路径。即使客观上转换任务更有利，当被描述为“重新开始”时，人们更倾向于避免这种选择。这种行为反映了人们对过去努力的重视和对“重新开始”的抵触。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“折返行为”现象及其相关研究的看法

不同观点：
• [florbnit] 认为科学家可能早已研究过“沉没成本谬误”，但为了将其包装为新发现而继续投入精力，而不是纠正结论。这暗示了对研究动机的怀疑。
• [scandox] 分享了个人经历，其配偶无法忍受“倒退以前进”的做法，甚至在规划跨国旅行时也需要直线前进，表明了对折返行为的强烈反感。
• [thelastgallon] 指出思考是困难的，一旦做出决定，重新评估需要大量精力，并认为持续质疑自己的决定是不切实际的。这强调了决策后坚持选择的合理性。
• [unsupp0rted] 提到了“撤销并恢复”选项的重要性，并指出某些工具训练用户克服对折返的厌恶，表明技术设计可以影响这种行为。
• [thelastgallon] 还提到在美国环境下，折返行为可能被视为可疑，并可能被监控，这引入了文化和社会背景对行为评价的影响。
• [7bit] 分享了个人体验，认为折返会让时间显得更慢，因此选择不折返，尽管承认这是个人感受，并不反驳研究结果。这突出了个体差异对行为的影响。
• [taneq] 从进化角度分析，认为在野外折返可能降低探索效率并增加暴露于捕食者的风险，表明这种行为在进化中可能被视为不利。
• [constantcrying] 批评将该现象称为“未识别的”是不准确的，因为这是行为心理学中广泛讨论的话题，并指出研究人员应该意识到相关理论，暗示对研究新颖性的质疑。
• [dcre] 仅表示对标题感到奇怪，没有深入讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该现象是否真的新颖及其研究动机是否正当。
• 不同评论者基于个人经验、技术设计、进化心理学和文化背景提供了多样化的视角。
• 个体差异和对折返行为的容忍度在讨论中被多次提及，强调了情境和个人偏好在决策中的重要性。

44624454.article_content:
Share on Twitter
Share on Facebook
Many people will continue with a longer, less efficient path to a goal rather than backtrack and take a shortcut — even when the backtracking would save time and effort. A new series of studies published in
Psychological Science
reveals that this behavior, called “doubling-back aversion,” emerges in both physical and mental tasks, and is driven not by mistaken cost estimates but by how people think about their past and future effort.
Psychologists have long studied why people stick with inefficient paths. The status quo bias describes the tendency to prefer current arrangements, while the sunk-cost fallacy highlights how people keep investing in failing efforts to justify past choices. But these don’t quite explain situations where people are choosing among equally new options — except that one feels like it erases what’s already been done.
Two researchers at UC Berkeley —
Kristine Y. Cho
, a PhD student, and
Clayton R. Critcher
, the Joe Shoong Professor of Business — sought to investigate whether people really do avoid doubling back, even when it’s objectively better, and to identify why.
“We both had a strong intuition that we kept circling back to as we developed our research,” Cho explained. “The idea was this: Imagine you’re walking from your house to a friend’s place. You leave your front door, turn left, and head down the block. But then you realize that you would get there faster if you had gone right instead.”
“At this point, you’re still close enough to home that retracing your steps, passing your front door, and taking the better route would actually save time. But would most people actually turn around and walk past where they started? We didn’t think so. That reluctance to reverse course, even when it’s clearly better, seemed to pop up a lot in real life. So we set out to investigate it.”
Across four experiments involving more than 2,500 adults from the United States, researchers tested whether people avoided more efficient strategies if they involved retracing their steps or restarting a task. The studies used both virtual navigation and cognitive tasks to examine the phenomenon in different contexts.
In the first study, college students used a virtual reality interface to move from one location to another. After walking a short distance, they encountered a map offering two paths to the destination. One path was shorter but required them to double back — literally reversing the steps they had just taken. Even though the shorter route would get them there faster, many avoided it when it required backtracking.
Subsequent studies replaced physical movement with mental effort. In one task, participants had to generate 40 words starting with the letter “G.” After listing 10, they were given a choice: continue with “G” words or switch to “T” words — a task expected to be easier. The tasks were objectively equivalent except for one difference: in one version, the new task was described as “starting over” and discarding previous work, while in the other version, it was described as “continuing the task under new instructions.” Both versions involved writing 30 more words, but only the “start over” version framed the switch as undoing progress.
In a third experiment, the researchers split doubling back into two components: deleting past work and having to complete the entire task from the beginning again. They manipulated how each component was framed and assessed how participants responded. The final study added a more detailed set of questions to examine how participants viewed their past and future efforts depending on their decision to switch tasks or stay the course.
Across all four studies, people consistently avoided options that involved doubling back, even when those options saved time. In the virtual reality study, only 31% of participants chose the shorter path when it required retracing their steps, compared to nearly 57% when it did not. In the word-generation tasks, framing the switch as “starting over” reduced the likelihood of switching from 75% to just 25%.
“The sheer size of the effect caught us off guard,” Cho told PsyPost. “For instance, take Study 2 in our paper. In that study, we told participants that they would have to list 40 words starting with the letter ‘G.’ But after they listed 10 words starting with ‘G’, we gave them the option to switch to listing words starting with the letter ‘T’. Because more words in the English language start with ‘T’ than ‘G’, switching essentially made the task easier. And when the choice was framed simply as a choice to switch letters for the remainder of the task, 75% of participants did indeed choose to switch to the easier task.”
“But when the choice was framed as ‘doubling back,’ that is, discarding their progress and starting over on a new task with 30 new ‘T’ words, only 25% switched. The contrast was so stark that my first reaction was to suspect a coding error, that maybe we had accidentally reversed th

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Oh-my-zsh 及其替代方案的性能、配置和使用体验

不同观点：
• **Oh-my-zsh 臃肿且影响性能**：soraminazuki 和 ivanjermakov 认为 Oh-my-zsh 给 zsh 带来了缓慢和臃肿的坏名声。他们指出，zsh 本身不需要配置框架或插件，只需要对默认设置做一些调整即可发挥其强大的自动补全功能。
   
• **轻量化自定义版本的 Oh-my-zsh**：srvmshr 分享了自己通过删除不必要的部分创建的 "leanZSH" 版本，并表示这种方法在旧机器上有效减少了启动时间。

• **使用替代框架**：
   - gregwebs 和 Jerry2 推荐使用 ZimFW 和 Prezto，因为它们在速度上优于 Oh-my-zsh，并且提供了更简洁的体验。
   - jauntywundrkind 提出了对不同 zsh 插件系统的比较需求，并分享了一些资源以供参考。

• **转向其他 shell**：
   - Sparkenstein 和 jpmonette 提到他们转向了 fish shell，并对其性能表示满意，尽管 fish 在插件和兼容 bash 方面可能存在一些问题。

• **手动配置和工具推荐**：
   - f311a 和 WhyNotHugo 分享了他们少于10行的自定义配置，并提到使用 fzf 和 starship 等工具可以替代许多插件。
   - OptionOfT 建议使用 uv 替代 pyenv 和 pyenv-virtualenv 以提升速度。

补充讨论：
• **compinit 缓存问题**：opk 讨论了在使用 oh-my-zsh 或其他插件框架时，正确设置 `compinit` 和缓存更新的重要性，以避免不必要的缓存重建。

• **Pure 和 Powerlevel10k 主题**：mcc1ane 提到了 Pure 主题，而其他用户在讨论中也涉及到 Powerlevel10k，显示出用户对美观和个性化配置的关注。

争议焦点：Oh-my-zsh 是否过于臃肿并影响性能，以及是否需要插件框架来有效配置 zsh。用户在选择替代方案时，主要关注速度和简化配置的需求。

data.title: Insights on Teufel’s first open-source speaker
data.author: lis
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了工业设计师Erik和电气工程师Jonathan开发MYND蓝牙音箱的幕后故事，强调了其耐用性和开源理念。MYND的设计聚焦于长寿命和可持续性，用户可以轻松更换电池，其他电子元件也易于替换，从而减少环境影响。音箱的材料选择和简约设计进一步优化了其生命周期评估（LCA）。开源设计允许用户根据公开数据自行制作和定制音箱部件，甚至可以通过3D打印制造塑料组件。尽管在声学设计上遇到一些挑战，团队成功平衡了易维修性与音质，确保消费者能获得高品质的音响体验。

• [KyleW9] 赞赏某款音箱的工业设计，特别是其降低CO² footprint的考量和易于维修的设计，尤其是电池部分。他还提到厂家提供了维修教程，认为这是为消费者着想的举措。

• [weinzierl] 认为Teufel是一个出色的公司，拥有卓越的音质和设计，赢得了多项奖项。然而，他认为MYND型号的外观设计不美观，特别是前面板的部分填充孔设计，给人一种已经磨损的感觉。他建议要么彻底走粗犷风格，要么保持干净设计。

44627158.article_content:
Industrial Designer Erik and Electrical Engineer Jonathan, two of the creative forces behind the new MYND Bluetooth speaker sat down with us for an interview to give fascinating insights into its development. They tell us how the
MYND
brings together
durability
and
Open-Source philosophy
in a way that allows consumers to let their imaginations run wild with customization ideas.
The Longer a Speaker is Used, the Lower its Environmental Impact.
Teufel Blog:
Erik & Jonathan, please introduce yourselves and tell us a bit about your roles in the development of the MYND.
Erik:
Gladly! I’m an industrial designer and I’m responsible for product design and implementation. Basically, I shepherd the project from initial concept all the way to final product.
Jonathan:
And I have been working on this project from the start as an electrical engineer. So I was involved from prototyping all the way to final components and PCB (printed circuit board) layout.
Teufel Blog:
The MYND is a product that was developed with a particular focus on long lifespan. What makes the MYND so durable?
Erik:
The fundamental idea behind the MYND is sustainability. The longer a speaker is used by the customer, the lower its CO² footprint, and thus its environmental impact. That was why it was very important for us that the MYND be very easy to repair. Even users without specialist knowledge can replace the battery no problem. We even published a tutorial. It’s hard to say today what technologies are going to become standard in the future, but we will try to be reactive to that and provide customers with components that will help facilitate new features.
The vision behind the MYND: Sustainability
Jonathan:
In terms of electronics, there are a number of factors that help prolong the MYND’s lifespan. For portable speakers, the battery is usually the first thing to fail. Usually, they can only last a few years. Best case scenario, users will then keep their speaker plugged in all the time. But in the worst, it ends up in the trash. The fact that the MYND’s battery is easy to replace is the first factor that makes it much more future proof. All electronic components of the MYND come from well-known producers and can be replaced either along with other components or individually, which makes repair very easy even when something does break.
Teufel Blog:
Which aspects of the MYND contribute to its positive Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)?
Erik:
The proper choice of materials, which should  either already be recycled, or be recyclable in the future. The construction and thus also design has to be condensed to the most essential elements, meaning keeping unnecessary features to a minimum because the less materials used, the better the LCA. Factors like ease of repair, which increases the lifetime of the speaker, can also have a positive effect.
Prototypes of the MYND
Teufel Blog:
When developing a product like the MYND, do you think more about what you personally would like to use, or what the customer would want?
Erik:
Product development is always a process of making a suitable product for our customers, not ourselves. The focus is thus clearly on the demands of our customers.
Jonathan:
In the best case, you can do both. Working on a product that you like and want to own yourself is an incredible motivator in terms of getting everything out of the product. Of course, you also can’t lose sight of what’s really important or get overly caught up on details. We always have colleagues around who are willing to offer different perspectives both from themselves and other target groups.
The MYND can be rebuilt from publicly available data.
Teufel Blog:
Open Source was also an important topic for the MYND. What does that mean for design and acoustics? Can you print some of the components at home in a 3D printer?
Jonathan:
We developed the drivers in-house, so the replacement parts for those are available only from Teufel. But if you instead use similar drivers, it is possible to build a whole MYND on your own using the data we published. You could produce the boards using our PCB diagrams, buy components from various retailers and assemble. A 3D printer with enough print volume and materials could print all the plastic parts, and we also have published the software the MYND uses internally. That means it needs only a handful of screws and you could build your very own speaker. You can also adjust the acoustic tuning to your personal wishes.
Teufel Blog:
Were there any compromises you had to make with the MYND’s acoustics to achieve the ease of repair, or were the aspects easy to harmonize?
Acoustic construction during production
Erik:
We were able to bring both aspects together very well, but it did present challenges at some points. For example, the grille on the front was supposed to be made of plastic. The shape and structure of the grille has a significant impact on the acoustics.
Teufel Blog:
What can customers expect from the MYND in terms of sound?

data.title: Master Foo and the Script Kiddie (1996)
data.author: RGBCube
data.article_summary: 一名来自Woot的年轻人自称想向Master Foo学习黑客技术，成为高手。Master Foo指引他去入侵一个安全措施薄弱的系统。年轻人照做后被捕入狱，几年后他回来责怪Master Foo。Master Foo再次给他一个IP地址，年轻人拒绝再犯法，此时他终于领悟到真正的智慧在于不滥用技术。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• [teddyh, BrenBarn, k2xl, nsb1, b3lvedere] - 这些评论主要分享或推荐类似的哲理故事和文献资源，如Unix Koans、The Codeless Code、Acts of Gord、Tao of Programming，以及Master Foo的故事。他们从积极的角度分享阅读体验和资源链接。

...and the Script Kiddie
A stranger from the land of Woot came to Master Foo as he was eating the morning meal
with his students.
âI hear y00 are very l33t,â he said. âPl33z teach m3 all y00 know.â
Master Foo's students looked at each other, confused by the stranger's barbarous language.
Master Foo just smiled and replied: âYou wish to learn the Way of Unix?â
âI want to b3 a wizard hax0r,â the stranger replied, âand 0wn ever3one's b0xen.â
âI do not teach that Way,â replied Master Foo.
The stranger grew agitated. âD00d, y00 r nothing but a p0ser,â he said. âIf y00 n00
anything, y00 wud t33ch m3.â
âThere is a path,â said Master Foo, âthat might bring you to wisdom.â The master scribbled
an IP address on a piece of paper. âCracking this box should pose you little difficulty, as
its guardians are incompetent. Return and tell me what you find.â
The stranger bowed and left. Master Foo finished his meal.
Days passed, then months. The stranger was forgotten.
Years later, the stranger from the land of Woot returned.
âDamn you!â he said, âI cracked that box, and it was easy like you said. But I got busted by
the FBI and thrown in jail.â
âGood,â said Master Foo. âYou are ready for the next lesson.â He scribbled an IP address on
another piece of paper and handed it to the stranger.
âAre you crazy?â the stranger yelled. âAfter what I've been through, I'm never going to
break into a computer again!â
Master Foo smiled. âHere,â he said, âis the beginning of wisdom.â
On hearing this, the stranger was enlightened.

data.title: Hacking a Toniebox
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了作者对Toniebox的破解和隐私问题。Toniebox是一种儿童音乐盒，通过放置NFC玩偶来播放云端的音频内容。作者指出，Toniebox需要联网和账户才能使用，且玩偶是专有的，无法在其他设备上使用。这让作者担心孩子的隐私，因为所有操作数据都会被记录并发送至服务器。作者通过拆解Toniebox，发现音频文件存储在内部SD卡上，并使用OPUS编码，未加密。通过工具如teddyBench，可以备份这些音频文件，以防将来无法访问。文章还提到，现代内容的“授权”模式让用户不再真正拥有这些内容，因此备份显得尤为重要。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• **Edd314159**：尽管有破解Toniebox的冲动，但由于其设计简单、孩子易于使用，以及担心家庭内部的反对，最终没有进行破解。强调了产品对儿童的友好性和家庭和谐的考虑。

• **alt227**：对Toniebox的设计和功能感到不满，特别是其限制性和物理设计问题（如玩偶易掉落）。转而使用Yoto播放器，认为其在设计和功能上优于Toniebox，尤其是在移动使用场景中。

• **maerch**：虽然承认Toniebox昂贵且有设计上的限制，但认为产品并非为成人设计，孩子对其非常喜爱。强调了Toniebox在孩子中的受欢迎程度和玩偶的玩具属性。

• **simgt**：选择了Yoto Mini，更喜欢卡片形式，并考虑使用标准NFC卡。但对需要连接WiFi而不是使用SD卡感到不满。

• **prmoustache**：提出使用Sony Minidiscs作为替代方案，强调其易用性和对孩子的友好性。

• **daft_pink**：对Toniebox和Yoto之间的选择感到犹豫，可能是因为两者都有各自的优缺点。

• **random_savv**：选择便宜的Sony录音/CD播放器，认为购买带有专有玩偶的音箱是疯狂的。

• **fxtentacle**：尽管不喜欢Toniebox的DRM，但认为它是最好的选择之一，特别是可以借用玩偶和公共图书馆的资源，且无广告和订阅。

• **kleiba**：指出Toniebox可以设置为离线模式，并通过路由器限制其网络访问，认为其对隐私的影响小于其他社交应用。

• **phars**：推荐开源项目Tonuino作为DIY替代方案，强调其可定制性和社区支持。

• **bj-rn**：提供另一个开源项目作为替代方案，并表示其侄女很喜欢。

• **pmg102**：选择Yoto是因为其支持自制卡片，可以自定义MP3文件或RSS链接。

• **wan888888**：提供了一个相关的技术逆向工程讨论链接。

• **harryscholes**：分享了自己开发的工具，用于下载播客并添加到Creative Tonie中。

补充讨论：
• **隐私问题**：一些用户对Toniebox的互联网连接和数据跟踪表示担忧，并提出了解决方案如离线模式和路由器限制。
• **替代方案**：多个评论提到了Yoto播放器和其他DIY项目如Tonuino和RPi-Jukebox-RFID，作为Toniebox的替代方案。
• **设计和功能**：用户对Toniebox的物理设计（如玩偶易掉落）和功能限制提出批评，同时也有人指出其孩子对产品的喜爱和易用性。
• **价格和专有性**：一些用户认为Toniebox过于昂贵，且其专有玩偶系统不够灵活。

争议焦点：
• **Toniebox的专有性和DRM**：一些用户对Toniebox的内容授权模式和DRM感到不满，认为其限制了使用自由。
• **设计问题**：特别是玩偶在移动使用中容易掉落的问题引起了用户的不满。

总体而言，讨论围绕Toniebox及其替代产品的优缺点展开，涉及设计、功能、隐私和价格等多个方面。

44627211.article_content:
Hack all the things - Toniebox
17. Jun 2025
Tags:
hacking
tonie
toniebox
Estimated reading time:
7 minutes
Continuing my
Hack all the things
series, I’m doing something slightly different today. So far I’ve hacked my PS Vita and Nintendo 3DS, but this time I want to talk about my Toniebox.
Or rather…my kids’ Toniebox.
If you’re unfamiliar with the thing, it’s a little music box with a built-in speaker, two little “ears” to raise or lower the volume and an NFC reader at the top. Instead of putting in cassettes or CDs (yes, I’m old!), you instead put little figurines (i.e. NFC tags) on top of the box. You can skim forwards and backwards by tilting the box (we never use that) and skip entire tracks by giving it a proper smack on the left or right.
These things come in multiple different colors.
Now, if you’re a bit familiar with NFC, you might be wondering where all the music is coming from. I don’t know how much information exactly an NFC tag can store, but it’s definitely way less than a 3h audio-play. And they are not using a crazy new compression algorithm either. They are using –
drumroll
–
the cloud
!
The ubiquitous cloud is also part of why I was against buying a Toniebox for the longest time. You need a Tonies account, otherwise the box is useless. The figurines are proprietary and cannot be used with any other hardware. As far as I know, there are no 3rd party “Tonies”.
The Toniebox needing an active internet connection also means that the company behind the Toniebox – Tonies SE – can theoretically track anything and everything my kids are doing with the box.
And of course it’s not a theory. Any interaction, putting on a figurine, slapping the box, using the ears, even playback progress, is recorded and sent out with a unique Toniebox ID – which of course is not anonymized and directly linked to your Tonies account.
However, the Toniebox connects to two URLs:
prod.de.tbs.toys
rtnl.bxcl.de
The first URL is used to authenticate with the Tonies servers and download music files to an internal SD card. The second one is used
only
for tracking. You can therefore blacklist
rtnl.bxcl.de
with a network wide ad blocker (e.g. Pi-Hole) to protect your kids privacy.
It’s neat that they’ve separated the URLs this clearly, but it sucks that they’re sending insane amounts of tracking information for a toy designed for and targeted at little kids. As a developer I get that having a lot of tracing information can be helpful to figure out those pesky bugs…but preferably I’d keep the privacy of little kids out of harms way.
Now the other problem with the cloud is that things no longer really
belong
to you. Games, movies, TV shows,
audio-plays
…nowadays everything is just “licensed” to you.
It might be a shot in the dark and it may never happen, but… I’ve noticed how my wife and I will often reminisce about cassettes and CDs (sometimes even LPs) we owned as kids and the audio-plays we grew up with. And we’d like to share these with our kids, now that they are the right age for them.
Good luck finding a working cassette player nowadays. All of ours are broken. But that’s not an issue, because pretty much our entire collections are gone too, lost to the inevitable decay of time (and overeager parents who cleaned them out, because “who listens to cassettes anymore!?”).
We managed to recover some of the things we loved from YouTube, but a few things remain only in our memories.
If and when my kids approach me twenty-plus years down the line with “Dad, do you remember this one audio-play about the little pirate and his crew” and want to share these stories with their kids, I want to be able to point them right at it and say “you’re looking for this!”
It’s highly unlikely that there will be Tonieboxes when I’ll have grandkids and even more unlikely that you’ll find compatible hardware and – most importantly – there’s almost zero chance that the files are still accessible in the Tonies cloud!
Luckily, you can just remove three screws, take the thing apart and pull out an SD card for some sweet backups.
I did some online research and eventually learned that the audio files are compressed with OPUS. They are not encrypted, so if you’ve got the codec installed, you should be able to open the “bigger” files on the SD card with something like
VLC
and play them right away.
There are some smaller files that contain metadata, e.g. how long individual tracks are. I ignored them in my own naive script, because I couldn’t figure out the metadata format.
However, after a few months someone on Mastodon
1
mentioned
this video from 37C3
2
(only in German). I found the talk incredibly interesting and informative. From there I also learned about
https://tonies-wiki.revvox.de/
and
teddyBench
.
teddyBench in particular is an amazing little tool. You can point it at a directory containing files from an Tonies SD card and it’ll show a grid with pictures of the figurines and can export the content. The kicker for me was that they managed to read the

data.title: Show HN: Conductor, a Mac app that lets you run a bunch of Claude Codes at once
data.author: Charlieholtz
data.article_summary: Conductor是一款用于在Mac上并行运行多个Claude Code代理的工具。它提供美观的用户界面，并自动处理git worktree操作。用户可以添加代码库，每个Claude Code代理有独立的工作空间，方便查看工作状态和代码变更。目前仅支持Claude Code，但未来将支持更多代理。Conductor利用用户已登录的Claude Code账户（API密钥或Pro/Max计划）进行支付。该工具由Melty Labs开发，广受好评，被视为AI编码辅助和代理编排的新篇章。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Conductor工具的功能、使用体验及其潜在改进

不同观点：
• [myflash13] 认为Conductor没有满足其对现有本地仓库进行简单git worktree管理的需求，反而要求Github权限并重新克隆仓库，导致需要重复安装依赖，增加了复杂性。该用户期望无需Github权限和依赖重装的简洁解决方案。
• [Samin100] 对工具的潜力表示兴奋，指出异步模型接口与现有同步聊天UI将有很大不同，并认为Claude Code在提供经济价值方面表现突出，未来界面改进空间大。
• [lachances] 关注Github权限问题，询问是否可以不要求对整个Github账户的写入权限。
• [aantix] 提到Conductor在文本输出和输入的体验上不如Claude Code，使用时缺乏愉悦感。
• [maxverse] 赞赏设计美学，并询问设计团队和设计风格的名称。
• [buremba] 提供了一些使用反馈，包括希望在对话中自由切换计划和执行模式，以及在终端中定义如何让Claude思考的方式。还提到希望通过任务列表提高效率，并分享了在Slack中运行Claude Code的实验。
• [lvl155] 对Claude Code变慢表示不满，认为新功能影响了普通用户的体验。
• [freedomben] 虽然认为自己不是目标用户，但觉得工具的想法不错，特别是在管理多个任务时，工具提供的仪表盘可能有用。不过目前使用tmux窗口也能满足需求。
• [jbentley1] 提到Crystal可以实现Conductor的所有功能，而且是开源的，提供了一个GitHub链接。
• [simonbw] 对Conductor表示赞赏，认为它解决了Claude Code工作流中的常见痛点，是一个干净简单的扩展。
• [lordnacho] 不理解Conductor的独特之处，询问直接打开新终端窗口启动Claude的区别。
• [davidbalbert] 询问Conductor是否支持通过Mac上的VS Code ssh远程在Linux桌面开发。
• [janpieterz] 喜欢工具的功能，但关心数据是否会发送到服务器，希望有更透明的信息。
• [abdullin] 询问Conductor是否类似于OpenAI Codex，提供隔离的环境运行每个代理。
• [rapatel0] 建议将Claude Code路由器智能集成到工具中，以帮助管理token预算和模型多路复用。

补充讨论：
• 用户对Conductor的Github权限要求、性能影响和设计美学有较多讨论。
• 部分用户关心工具是否开源以及对不同开发环境的支持。
• 一些用户对Conductor的功能改进提出了具体建议，如任务列表、仪表盘和集成Claude Code路由器等。
• 争议的焦点在于Conductor是否真正简化了工作流以及对Github权限的要求是否合理。

data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了AI研究中两种方法的平衡问题：基于“人类知识”的方法和依赖“数据+计算”的通用方法。作者反对Rich Sutton在“苦涩的教训”一文中提出的观点，即仅依靠数据和计算就能取得长期进展，认为人类知识和数据驱动方法需要相互补充和平衡。文章指出，没有纯粹依赖人类知识或完全无需人类指导的机器学习模型。人类知识在模型构建的各个阶段，从设计到评估，都发挥着重要作用。尽管随着技术发展，模型可能更多依赖“有影响力的”方法，但人类知识的直接应用仍然不可或缺。作者以大型语言模型为例，说明在模型生命周期的不同阶段，如何平衡这两种方法以构建有效的AI模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“苦涩的教训”（The Bitter Lesson）的不同理解和争议

不同观点：
• [aabhay] 认为“苦涩的教训”背后还有更“苦涩的现实”，即虽然可以通过增加计算资源和数据来扩展模型，但要得到高质量的模型，仍需要大量人工筛选和标注的高质量数据。现代最好的模型背后是数十亿计的资金投入，用于获取和处理这些数据。

• [rdw] 提出“苦涩的教训”之所以令人失望，是因为AI研究人员原本希望通过构建类似人类智能的系统来理解人类智能，而不仅仅是构建一个有效的“黑箱”模型。这一教训反映了在未完全理解智能的情况下构建智能系统的无奈。

• [rhet0rica] 质疑“苦涩的教训”的普遍性，指出历史上确实存在基于纯人类知识构建的专家系统（如MYCIN），因此认为该教训并未充分考虑已有研究成果，并批评相关讨论缺乏研究深度。

• [rhaps0dy] 认为Sutton的“苦涩的教训”讨论的是AI的长期进展，而不是短期生产需求。短期内，手动添加一些知识对模型仍然重要，但长期来看，这种方法对推动AI进步作用有限。

• [macawfish] 强调“苦涩的教训”核心在于更多依赖机器学习而非人工调整，有效利用已有数据，而不是简单地通过增加计算和数据来解决问题。

• [roadside_picnic] 结合自身经验指出，在实际工作中，数据往往比架构和基础设施更具限制性。在数据不足的情况下，简单且可解释的模型往往比复杂的神经网络模型更有效。他主张根据问题的信息量选择合适的模型。

• [godelski] 认为虽然“规模就是一切”的观点是错误的，但规模的增加确实带来了显著进步。然而，AI的发展不仅仅依赖于规模，还需要算法创新、数据收集方式的改进等。他强调AI领域仍有大量创新空间。

• [grillitoazul] 指出“苦涩的教训”仅在一定范围内有效。例如，LLM在处理某些特定任务（如大数相加）时表现不如传统算法，表明在某些情境下，仍需要新的智能算法来突破现有局限。

• [littlestymaar] 通过Leela Chess Zero与Stockfish的案例说明，结合计算资源和人类知识可以取得最佳效果。虽然纯粹依赖计算资源可以取得进展，但同时拥有计算资源和人类知识的方案往往更具优势。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于“苦涩的教训”是否适用于所有情境，尤其是当前模型是否仅通过增加数据和计算资源就能取得最佳效果，还是需要结合人类知识和智能算法。
• 讨论中多次提到数据质量和模型可解释性的重要性，尤其是在实际应用中，简单模型在数据有限的情况下可能比复杂模型更有效。
• 有人质疑“苦涩的教训”是否被过度简化和误解，历史上的专家系统被作为反例提出。
• 总体上，讨论反映了对AI发展路径的多元看法，从依赖规模到结合人类知识和智能算法，不同观点强调了不同因素的重要性。

44626789.article_content:
“The Bitter Lesson” is wrong. Well… sort of.
Assaf Pinhasi
3 min read
·
Just now
--
Listen
Share
TL;DR
There is no dichotomy between domain knowledge vs. “general purpose methods that leverage data+compute”.
They are both powerful tools that compensate for each other and need to be balanced and traded off during the model building process.
“The bitter lesson” in 30 seconds
“The bitter lesson”
is one of the most popular opinion pieces about AI research and it’s future.
In his writing, Rich Sutton makes a dichotomy between two main schools of AI research:
1. Research based on “human knowledge”
2. Research based on scaling methods like “learning and search” that scale with more data and compute.
Sutton claims that virtually all long term progress in AI was achieved using the latter, and that the former is actually detrimental and distracting.
He continues to provide multiple very convincing examples.
The false conclusion
Many people who have read the post reach the conclusion that “you don’t need human knowledge, just use methods that rely on data + compute”.
I don’t believe the dichotomy can exist in reality.
Counter-argument
No machine learning model was ever built using
pure
“human knowledge” — because then it wouldn’t be a learning model.
It would be a hard coded algorithm.
Similarly, no machine learning model was ever created
without
any
“human knowledge” because 1) models are still designed by humans which made design decisions and 2) models cannot learn useful things without human guidance.
We have no reason to believe that models that “ search and learn” at huge scale as a black box will magically align to be useful to humans
Evaluating models is an integral part of the model development lifecycle and as such needs to be accounted for in the discussion about “human knowledge” vs. “search and learn”.
Do I sound like the dude on the left? I hope not!
Alternative theory
The entire model building process is guided by domain knowledge.
Methods which apply this knowledge range from “
direct
” to “
influential
”
On the “
direct
” end of the spectrum, we codify the knowledge explicitly. Knowledge can be seen directly in the code or data.
On the “
influential
” end of the spectrum, we create some derivative or translation between the domain model and the model’s behavior, and apply them at well selected “pressure points” to guide the model’s behavior.
We need to choose the “operating point” on the spectrum multiple times, for different parts of the model lifecycle.
Often when we choose a more “
influential
” approach early on, we end up needing to use more “
direct
” methods later in the lifecycle, especially evaluation
This is needed because giving the model higher degrees of freedom increases risk of it learning catastrophic behaviors, given that it’s learning process is not at all aligned to human-centric thinking process.
It’s possible that the sum total of investment in domain knowledge related tasks has not changed so dramatically over time.
What may have changed is how this investment is distributed across the model building lifecycle.
Example
An example can be seen in lifecycle of building LLMs.
We start off with very broad “influential” approach, and slowly increase how “explicit” we are with our domain knowledge and judgement:
Self-supervision on massive scale, highly varied datasets
Curated datasets in sub-domains in which we want the model to be better (e.g. textbooks, coding competitions, etc.)
Human feedback, labels and preferences
Guardrails and various alignment techniques
Evaluation with highly curated domain specific data and tools — from domain-rich judge prompts, to code execution environment, high quality datasets labeled by experts, red-teaming, etc.
Summary
It’s possible that over time, as we find more ways to provide models with huge scale supervision that will allow us to shift further towards the “influential” end of the spectrum .
However, I don’t expect this will happen suddenly — rather it will be a very long process.
For now, and in the foreseeable future, domain-knowledge remains a critical part in building useful AI models.

data.title: Laminar Flow Airfoil
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了层流翼型及其在航空领域的应用。层流是指空气在飞机机翼或机身表面平滑、无干扰地流动，对飞行至关重要。如果流动被中断，会产生湍流，导致升力下降和阻力增加。层流翼型设计旨在保持边界层的平滑流动，以减少阻力。

北美P-51“野马”战斗机是首款有意采用层流翼型的飞机，但由于制造表面不够光滑，实际层流效果有限。贝尔P-63“眼镜王蛇”也有类似问题。层流理论可追溯到德国空气动力学家路德维希·普朗特的研究，他提出了边界层的概念。

尽管“ consolidated B-24解放者”的“戴维斯”翼型早于P-51就具有低阻力特性，但设计者并未意识到它是层流翼型。NACA在20世纪30年代末对一些飞机进行了层流翼型测试，如改装的B-18。

层流翼型的应用需要极高的表面光滑度，这在批量生产中难以实现。北美航空通过填充和涂漆来解决这一问题，以提供必要的平滑度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同飞行器中的创新技术，特别是与 laminar flow（层流）相关的设计及其实际效果

不同观点：
• [K0balt] 分享了其驾驶 Aero Commander 100 "Darter" 的个人经验。他提到该飞机的两个创新设计：纤维玻璃叶簧起落架和层流翼型。他指出，层流翼型在巡航时相比 Cessna 172 有 0.5-1 加仑每小时的燃油效率提升。然而，K0balt 也提到该飞机不适合 bush flying（丛林飞行），因为在地面效应中加速效果不佳。此外，他还提到失速特性，指出飞机失速时表现温和，不易突然下坠。

• [upofadown] 通过其滑翔俱乐部的经历，讨论了层流对滑翔机性能的影响。他提到一个名为 "BUGS" 的开关，用于在昆虫污染破坏层流时调整飞行计算机的计算参数。这种污染会导致局部层流破坏，进而影响滑翔机的性能，尤其是在最终滑翔计算中。如果没有及时调整，可能会导致飞行员对所需高度的误判。

• [ks1723] 提到在2000年代初期，即使经过几十年的研发，仍然有新型层流机翼和机身在商务喷气机（如 HondaJet）上的应用空间。他引用了 HondaJet 的技术文档链接，强调了该机型在气动设计上的创新。

补充讨论：
• 层流技术在不同飞行器中的具体应用和效果：K0balt 强调了层流在小型螺旋桨飞机中的燃油效率提升，而 upofadown 则指出了层流在滑翔机中受外部污染影响的敏感性。

• 技术进步的持续性：ks1723 提到即使在现代航空技术发展多年后，层流技术仍然有创新的空间，显示出该技术在不同机型中的持续应用和研究价值。

争议焦点：虽然没有直接争议，但不同飞行器对层流技术的依赖程度和实际效果存在差异。K0balt 对 Aero Commander 100 在 bush flying 中的表现有所保留，而 upofadown 则强调了层流在滑翔机中受环境因素影响的敏感性。

Laminar Flow Airfoil
Laminar Flow
is the smooth, uninterrupted flow of
air over the contour of the wings, fuselage, or other
parts of an aircraft in flight. Laminar flow is most
often found at the front of a streamlined body and is
an important factor in flight. If the smooth flow of
air is interrupted over a wing section, turbulence is
created which results in a loss of
lift
and a high
degree of drag. An airfoil designed for minimum
drag
and uninterrupted flow of the boundary layer is called
a laminar airfoil.
The Laminar flow theory dealt with the development
of a symmetrical airfoil section which had the same
curvature on both the upper and lower surface. The
design was relatively thin at the leading edge and progressively
widened to a point of greatest thickness as
far aft as possible. The theory in using an airfoil of
this design was to maintain the adhesion of the boundary layers of
airflow which are present in flight as far
aft of the leading edge as possible. On normal airfoils,
the boundary layer would be interrupted at high speeds
and the resultant break would cause a turbulent flow
over the remainder of the foil. This turbulence would
be realized as drag up the point of maximum speed, at
which time the control surfaces and aircraft flying
characteristics would be affected. The formation of the
boundary layer is a process of layers of air formed
one next to the other, i.e.; the term laminar is derived
from the lamination principle involved.
The History of Laminar Flow
The
North American P-51 Mustang
was the first aircraft intentionally
designed to use laminar flow airfoils.  However, wartime National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA) research
data shows that Mustangs were not manufactured with a sufficient
degree of surface quality to maintain much laminar flow on the wing.  The
Royal Air Force (RAF) found that the
Bell P-63 Kingcobra
, despite being designed with laminar airfoils,
also was not manufactured with sufficient surface quality to have much
laminar flow.
The
Mustang
was a mathematically designed airplane
and the wing foil that was to be classified as a
"semi-empirical venture" by the British was cleared for
adoption on the new design. The wing section would
be the only part of the fighter which would be tested
in a wind tunnel prior to the first test flight. Due to the
speculation of the success of the radical foil, the engineering
department was committed to adopt a more
conventional airfoil within thirty days of the tests in
the event the wing did not come up to specifications.
A one quarter scale model of the wing was designed
and constructed for tests in the wing tunnel at the
California Institute of Technology.
The use of this airfoil on the
Mustang
would greatly
add to the drag reducing concept that was paramount
in all design phases of the airplane. The few applications
of this foil, prior to this time, had been handbuilt
structures which were finished to exacting
tolerances. An absolutely smooth surface was necessary
due to the fact that any surface break or rough
protrusion would interrupt the airflow and detract from
the laminar flow theory. Because of the exactness
required, the foil had been shelved by other manufacturers
due to the clearances and tolerances which are
used in mass production. The engineers at North American Aviation (NAA)
approached this problem with a plan to fill and paint
the wing surface to provide the necessary smoothness.
The foil which was used for the Mustang had a
thickness ratio of 15.1 percent at the wing root at 39
percent of the chord. The tip ratio was 11.4 percent
at the 50 percent chord line. These figures provided
the maximum thickness area at 40 percent from the
leading edge of the wing and resulted in a small negative
pressure gradient over the leading 50-60 percent
of the wing surface.
The
Consolidated B-24 Liberator
"Davis" airfoil was also a laminar flow airfoil,
which predates the Mustang's.  However, the designers of the B-24 only
knew that their airfoil had very low drag in the wind tunnel.  They did
not realize that it was a laminar flow airfoil.
There were several aircraft modified by NACA, in the late 1930s,
to have laminar flow test sections on their wings.  Hence, such aircraft
as a modified B-18 were some of the first aircraft to fly with laminar
flow airfoils.
The boundary layer concept is credited to the great German
aerodynamicist, Ludwig Prandtl.  Prandtl hypothesized and proved the
existence of the boundary layer long before the
Mustang
was a gleam in
anyone's eye.
Example:
First, let's get more specific about what laminar flow is.  The
flow next to any surface forms a
boundary layer
, as the flow has zero
velocity right at the surface and some distance out from the surface it
flows at the same velocity as the local
outside
flow.  If this boundary
layer flows in parallel layers, with no energy transfer between layers, it
is laminar.  If there is energy transfer, it is turbulent.

• [upofadown] 通过其滑翔俱乐部的经历，讨论了层流对滑翔机性能的影响。他提到一个名为 "BUGS" 的开关，用于在昆虫污染破坏层流时调整飞行计算机的计算参数。这种污染会导致局部层流破坏，进而影响滑翔机的性能，尤其是在最终滑翔计算中。如果没有及时调整，可能会导致飞行员对所需高度的误判。

• [ks1723] 提到在2000年代初期，即使经过几十年的研发，仍然有新型层流机翼和机身在商务喷气机（如 HondaJet）上的应用空间。他引用了 HondaJet 的技术文档链接，强调了该机型在气动设计上的创新。

补充讨论：
• 层流技术在不同飞行器中的具体应用和效果：K0balt 强调了层流在小型螺旋桨飞机中的燃油效率提升，而 upofadown 则指出了层流在滑翔机中受外部污染影响的敏感性。

• 技术进步的持续性：ks1723 提到即使在现代航空技术发展多年后，层流技术仍然有创新的空间，显示出该技术在不同机型中的持续应用和研究价值。

争议焦点：虽然没有直接争议，但不同飞行器对层流技术的依赖程度和实际效果存在差异。K0balt 对 Aero Commander 100 在 bush flying 中的表现有所保留，而 upofadown 则强调了层流在滑翔机中受环境因素影响的敏感性。

he earthquake shook us awake at 4:31 in the morning. We hurried into a closet while, for fifteen seconds, it finished its business and the car alarms down on Third and California began their complaint. And suddenly there was a rip in time, a twenty-heartbeat glimpse into the equally inhuman roll of ages where continents join and break apart.

The geology of the Transverse Ranges consists largely of granite from the Mesozoic Eraâ66Â to 252Â million years agoâwith some even earlier Precambrian material, at least 1.6Â billion years old.
These are large numbers. They belong to the calculus of deep time as introduced to the world by British scientists in the mid-nineteenth centuryânamely, the preeminent geologist of the age, Charles Lyell, and Charles Darwin, who borrowed Lyellâs unbounded temporality and used it to underpin his theory of evolution.
Long before he formulated that theory, Darwin himself had witnessed what he called âthe forces which slowly and by little starts uplift continents.â The year was 1835 and Darwin was near

the HMSÂ
Beagle.
In Chile, he was onshore one February day taking a nap when the ground began to rock. The quake lasted two minutes; its only local effect was to make Darwin âalmost giddy.â
Nearly two weeks later, he arrived in ConcepciÃ³n to find a completely ruined city. still adhering to the rocks,
ten feet above high-water mark.â Later that month, Darwin climbed high into the Andes, where he found âshells which were once crawling on the bottom of the sea, now standing nearly 14,000 feet above its level.â It had taken about twenty-five million years for those shells to reach that height.
For several years now, I have been reading these early theorists, thinking that their vision of geological and evolutionary time might give me a context for understanding not just the age of mountains but something more current. These days, geological forces, formerly the stuff of earthquakes and volcanoes, have escaped the confines of deep time to present themselves daily, winter, spring, summer, and fall.
It is on this other end of the scale of timeâin seasons rather than eonsâthat my own interest in natural science began and where today it finds its focus and concern. 主要讨论点：数据中心（DCs）的能源消耗及其环境影响

不同观点：
• [blibble] 认为，减少个人层面的能源消耗（如减少牛肉消费、减少驾驶和出国度假）并不会真正改善环境，因为大型科技公司（如亚马逊）仍在扩建数据中心，最终只是让这些公司高层（如贝索斯）更加富裕，而普通人变得无关紧要。

• [breakyerself] 指出，能源需求的增长是正常的，当前的环境问题更多是由于长期政策失败导致的，而不是单纯由个人或企业的行为所造成。

• [tootie] 提出一个技术性建议，询问为什么数据中心不采用地源热泵进行气候控制，因为这种方法的运营成本最低，可能有助于减少能源消耗。

Amazon’s Emissions Climbed 6% in 2024 on Data Center Buildout
Amazon’s Emissions Climbed 6% in 2024 on Data Center Buildout
The e-commerce giant emitted 68 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent last year, up 6% from 2024.
Matt Day
,
Bloomberg News
July 17, 2025
1 Min
Read
Image: Bloomberg
(Bloomberg) -- Amazon’s carbon emissions rose for the first time in three years in 2024, driven by data center construction and fuel consumption by its delivery providers.
The world’s largest online retailer emitted 68.25 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent last year, up 6% from the prior year, Amazon said in its annual
sustainability report
, which was published on Wednesday. The company’s emissions last year were up by a third since Amazon pledged in 2019 to eliminate them by 2040.
The company and its high-tech rivals are spending heavily on data centers to power artificial intelligence applications, which require plenty of concrete and steel, two materials that use a lot of energy to produce.
Environmental watchdogs have raised the alarm as the AI data center boom helped supercharge electricity demand, and, in some areas, breathed new life into
natural gas
and
coal-fired power
. Those energy sources had fallen out of favor among tech companies in recent years as they pledged to find cleaner sources and zero out their impact on carbon emissions.
Amazon and fellow data-center giants Alphabet, Meta Platforms, and Microsoft have also signed deals to scoop up carbon-free nuclear power in the coming years.
Amazon’s emissions from purchased electricity rose 1% last year, the first increase since the company began reporting the figure in 2019, “in part due to the higher electricity usage required to support advanced technologies.”
Related:
Data Center Emissions: Virginia, Texas, California Top CO2 Chart
“This underscores why it’s important to scale carbon-free energy sources to continue to deliver the advanced technologies our customers need,” Amazon said in the report.

data.title: The great AI delusion is falling apart
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了人工智能（AI）在实际应用中的表现与公众期望之间的差距。一项随机对照试验显示，尽管程序员认为使用AI工具能提高20%的编码速度，但实际上他们反而慢了19%。这种自我欺骗的现象广泛存在，许多人愿意相信AI能带来巨大生产力提升，尽管现实往往相反。多项研究和调查表明，AI项目的投资回报率低，失败率高，且经常无法完成任务。企业和媒体夸大AI的能力，部分是为了削减成本和提升股价。专家指出，当前的AI模型不够成熟，无法自主实现复杂商业目标，且存在推理能力不足等问题。文章认为，公众对AI的盲目信仰源于误导性宣传和自我欺骗。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对论文中警示的误解是否应该被公开传播

不同观点：
• 一方认为将论文中明确警示的误解进行公开传播（如刊登在报纸上）是不妥的。这可能导致公众对研究的错误理解，从而产生误导性的结论。该观点强调应尊重作者的提醒，避免误用研究结果。

Is the secret of artificial intelligence that we have to kid ourselves, like an audience at a magic show?
Some fascinating new research suggests that self-deception plays a key role in whether AI is perceived to be a success or a dud.
In a randomised controlled trial – the first of its kind – experienced computer programmers could use AI tools to help them write code. What the trial revealed was a vast amount of self-deception.
“The results surprised us,” research lab METR reported. “Developers thought they were 20pc faster with AI tools, but they were actually 19pc
slower
when they had access to AI than when they didn’t.”
In reality, using AI made them
less
productive: they were wasting more time than they had gained. But what is so interesting is how they swore blind that the opposite was true.
If you think AI is helping you in your job, perhaps it’s because you
want
to believe that it works.
Since OpenAI’s ChatGPT was thrown open to the general public in late 2022, pundits have been forecasting huge productivity gains from deploying AI. They hope that it will supercharge growth and boost GDP. This has become the default opinion in high-status policy circles.
But all this techno-optimism is founded on delusion. The “lived experience” of using real tools in the real world paints a very different picture.
The past few days have felt like a turning point, as the reluctance of pointing out the emperor’s new clothes diminishes.
“I build AI agents for a living, it’s what I do for my clients,” wrote one Reddit user. “The gap between the hype and what’s actually happening on the ground is turning into a canyon”
AI isn’t reliable enough to do the job promised. According to an IBM survey of 2,000 chief executives, three out of four AI projects have failed to show a return on investment, which is a remarkably high failure rate.
Don’t hold your breath for a white-collar automation revolution either: AI agents fail to complete the job successfully about 65 to 70pc of the time, according to a study by Carnegie Mellon University and Salesforce.
The analyst firm Gartner Group has concluded that “current models do not have the maturity and agency to autonomously achieve complex business goals or follow nuanced instructions over time.” Gartner’s head of AI research Erick Brethenoux says: “AI is not doing its job today and should leave us alone”.
It’s no wonder that companies such as Klarna, which laid off staff in 2023 confidently declaring that AI could do their jobs, are hiring humans again.
This is extraordinary, and we can only have reached this point because of a historic self-delusion. People will even pledge their faith to AI working well despite their own subjective experience to the contrary, the AI critic Professor Gary Marcus noted last week.
“Recognising that it sucks in your own speciality, but imagining that it is somehow fabulous in domains you are less familiar with”, is something he calls “ChatGPT blindness”.
Much of the news is misleading. Firms are simply using AI as an excuse for retrenchment. Cost reduction is the big story in business at the moment.
Globally, President Trump’s erratic behaviour has induced caution, while in the UK,
business confidence is at “historically depressed levels”
, according to the Institute of Directors, reeling from Reeves’s autumn taxes. Attributing those lay-offs to technology is simply clever PR, and helps boost the share price.

data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了两个经济现象。首先，美国年轻男性大学毕业生的失业率在过去一年中从不到5%上升至7%，与未获得学位的同龄人失业率持平，而女性毕业生的失业率没有明显变化。尽管初步推测这可能与人工智能导致的就业岗位减少有关，但数据表明，入门级编程和软件开发岗位的招聘正在回升，早期的编码职业就业情况甚至优于人工智能时代之前。

其次，文章分析了加州快餐行业最低工资从16美元提高到20美元的影响。研究显示，这一政策使得加州快餐行业的工资上涨约8%，但就业人数相对其他地区减少了2%到4%，相当于减少了18,000个工作岗位。

文章还提到其他相关研究，探讨了最低工资政策对就业市场的影响以及大学毕业生失业率上升的现象。

Rising Graduate Joblessness Is Mainly Affecting Men. Will That Last?
John Burn-Murdoch
Financial Times
Date Posted:
July 18, 2025
Is Database:
Database
The unemployment rate for recent male college graduates (22–27) has risen from <5% to 7%. Recent male graduates “are now unemployed at the same rate as their non-graduate counterparts,” while the rate for their female peers is unchanged.
Share
Summary
Related
Topics
More
PDF
The unemployment rate for recent male graduates has risen steeply from less than 5% to 7% over the past 12 months. For young female graduates in the US, joblessness is unchanged over the same period, if not falling slightly. Most striking of all, recently graduated young men are now unemployed at the same rate as their non-graduate counterparts, completely erasing the college employability premium. At first glance, this lines up neatly with the theory that we’re looking at the leading edge of a wave of AI-driven job displacement. But drill down into sector-specific employment, and the evidence doesn’t seem to fit the narrative. The much-remarked-upon contraction in hiring entry-level programmers and software developers in the US has sharply reversed in recent months. In fact, relative to the pre-generative AI era, early-career coding employment is now tracking ahead of the rest of the economy.

Educated but Unemployed, a Rising Reality for College Grads
and
Something Alarming Is Happening To The Job Market

Did California's Fast Food Minimum Wage Reduce Employment?
Jeffrey Clemens, Olivia Edwards and Jonathan Meer
National Bureau of Economic Research
Date Posted:
July 16, 2025
Is Database:
Database
The 2024 rise in CA’s minimum wage in fast food restaurants from $16 to $20 raised the sector’s wages ~8% and lowered its employment by 2 to 4% relative to the US sector overall, with an estimated loss of 18,000 CA fast food jobs. @jeffreypclemens
Share
Summary
Related
Topics
More
PDF
We analyze the effect of California's $20 fast food minimum wage [up from $16], which was enacted in September 2023 and went into effect in April 2024, on employment in the fast food sector. We document that AB 1228 increased wages substantially, with a roughly 8% increase in California’s fast food sector relative to the fast food sector elsewhere in the country. In unadjusted data from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, we find that employment in California's fast food sector declined by 2.7% relative to employment in the fast food sector elsewhere in the United States from September 2023 through September 2024. In Figures 1b, 1c, and 1d, for which each series has been indexed relative to September 2023, the magnitude of the relative decline through late 2024 is readily observed from the graphs as being on the order of 2 to 4%. Indexing, detrending, and seasonally adjusting the data make the series more visually comparable but do not substantively alter the relative movements that underlie our regression estimates. Our median estimate translates into a loss of 18,000 jobs in California's fast food sector relative to the counterfactual.

data.title: Nobody knows how to build with AI yet
data.author: Stwerner
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在编程和软件开发中的应用及其影响

不同观点：
• **Tom_m**：认为AI应帮助开发者专注于高层次的设计和批判性思维，而非纠结于代码细节。他强调软件架构和设计模式的重要性，并指出掌握这些技能需要长时间的经验积累。
• **Nirvanatikku**：赞同文章观点，强调清晰表达问题对AI驱动开发的重要性。他分享了使用Repl.it等工具的积极体验，认为这些工具能提升开发效率，但也指出AI有时会偏离预期，需要人工干预。
• **Lordnacho**：享受AI辅助编程带来的便利，特别是减少了繁琐的编辑工作，提高了工作效率。他认为AI对有经验的开发者特别有帮助，但对新手的影响尚不明确。
• **Rmdashrfv**：指出AI在实现细节上的局限性，尤其是在非web领域的软件开发中。他认为AI的成功很大程度上依赖于开发者对实现细节的不关心，且很多项目因无法精确控制AI而失败。
• **Flatcircle**：认为AI是搜索技术的进化，只是一个工具，不会导致行业的存在危机。他强调聪明的人能利用工具做很多有趣的事情，但工具仍需人工操作。
• **D00mB0t**：以戏谑的方式提到利用AI在网络安全咨询方面赚钱的潜力。
• **Sgt101**：分享了在使用AI模型时的经验，指出在处理已知任务时效果较好，但在不熟悉的领域容易产生错误且难以纠正。
• **Schneems**：关注AI生成代码的质量和一致性问题，认为当前AI在将开放问题分解为可验证的具体步骤方面表现不佳，希望有更多控制权。
• **Gngoo**：认为自己已经掌握了利用AI高效开发的技巧，但难以传授给他人。他强调AI对开发效率的巨大提升，但指出多数开发者尚未接受这种新方式。
• **Asadotzler**：质疑AI在处理安全、国际化、可访问性等软件质量核心问题上的能力，认为业余开发者难以达到商业软件的标准，AI辅助开发方式可能阻碍行业成熟。
• **Divan**：强调阅读和理解代码的重要性，认为即使有AI辅助，开发者仍需保持对代码的清晰理解，以确保代码对其他开发者友好。
• **Saadatq**：提出“flex coding”的新概念，分享了利用AI在短时间内高效完成项目的个人经验，强调AI对生活工作平衡的积极影响。
• **Siliconc0w**：对AI开发的效果感到失望，认为AI指导可能影响下一代开发者的能力发展，并担心当前方法可能对行业产生负面影响。
• **Wiremine**：分享了对AI辅助开发的积极体验，认为这是一种新的方法论，可能导致一些热爱手工艺的开发者离开行业，但同时也会开启新的机会。

补充讨论：
• **AI对开发效率的影响**：多数开发者认为AI能提高效率，尤其是在处理已知问题和繁琐任务时，但对新手和复杂项目的适用性仍存在争议。
• **AI生成代码的质量和一致性**：开发者普遍关注AI生成代码的质量问题，强调人工干预和代码审查的必要性。
• **AI对开发者角色的影响**：一些开发者担心AI可能导致开发者角色的转变，从代码编写者变为AI管理员，可能影响行业的人才培养和职业发展。
• **AI在非web领域软件开发中的局限性**：部分开发者指出AI在处理非web领域软件开发任务时表现不佳，实现细节和特定需求仍需人工处理。

data.title: Adblockers stop publishers serving ads to (or even seeing) 1B web users
data.author: thm
data.article_summary: 根据Ad-Shield的报告，"暗流量"（即被严格广告拦截器隐藏的网页浏览量）在过去三年中增长了49%。这些拦截器屏蔽所有网站分析、白名单广告、请求允许广告的弹窗、cookie提示以及付费墙等。全球有9.76亿用户产生"暗流量"，占所有网络流量的18%，预计2026年将达到11亿用户。英国23%的网络流量为"暗流量"，涉及1600万用户。多数用户并未主动选择屏蔽广告，而是由第三方如雇主、教育机构或安全软件启用。最令用户反感的广告是预播视频广告，半数受访者表示其令人沮丧。报告强调，广告拦截已成主流，对出版商收入构成威胁。同时，新闻/媒体联盟宣布取缔绕过付费墙的12ft.io网站。业内人士指出，理解并应对这一变化对出版商至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：广告拦截器及其对广告技术（adtech）和内容发布者的影响

不同观点：
• [veeti] 认为广告拦截器并不会完全阻止流量测量，因为发布者仍然可以通过服务器端日志进行测量。问题在于发布者过度依赖容易被绕过的JavaScript跟踪器。
• [stop50] 反驳“未经用户同意的去货币化”的说法，指出使用广告拦截器是用户的选择，且广告变得令人厌烦和侵犯隐私，是用户采用广告拦截器的主要原因。
• [altairprime] 提到在没有广告拦截器的情况下，某些网站会弹出冗长的法律条款弹窗，迫使用户接受。
• [general1726] 分享个人经历，说明广告商的激进策略迫使他们使用广告拦截器，形成了恶性循环。
• [ethin] 表示对广告技术公司面临的困境感到满意，认为他们是咎由自取，广告拦截器是在阻止他们的不当行为。
• [3036e4] 使用NoScript来阻止大部分广告和跟踪脚本，并表示如果广告没有跟踪行为，可以接受。
• [musicale] 强调广告技术的激进和讨厌是用户采用广告拦截器的主要驱动因素，并指出安全风险也是原因之一。
• [D-Coder] 质疑如何测量所谓的“无法测量的流量”，并暗示广告技术公司可能有意高估这种流量。
• [southernplaces7] 对广告拦截器减少寄生数据采集表示满意，并直接对数据采集公司表示不满。
• [ok123456] 质疑“暗流量”的概念，将其与用户在电视上跳过广告的行为相比较。
• [bediger4000] 认为广告拦截器提高了网络安全性，是个人信息安全的一部分。
• [debarshri] 提醒用户注意随机安装的广告拦截器可能获取私人信息，并提出广告拦截器可以作为订阅管理平台的机会。

补充讨论：
• [pinum] 引用数据指出，大量用户通过广告了解并激活了硬广告拦截器。

争议焦点：
• 广告拦截器的使用是否经过用户同意，以及其对广告生态系统的影响。
• 广告技术公司和发布者是否应为激进广告策略导致的后果负责。
• “暗流量”概念的合理性和测量方法的有效性。

这些观点反映了广告拦截器在用户隐私、安全和广告生态系统中的复杂角色，以及各方对此的不同看法。

44627358.article_content:
AdGuard, a strict ad-blocker and privacy protection app. Picture: Shutterstock/mariakray
Web traffic that cannot be measured, and therefore monetised, by publishers has grown by 49% in the past three years, according to a new report.
The new study from adtech company Ad-Shield claims to be the first to comprehensively measure and explain the scale of “dark traffic”.
“Dark traffic” is defined as page views hidden to publishers by the strictest types of ad-blockers.
These block all on-site analytics, whitelisted adverts, ad-block walls that ask people to allow ads, cookie content pop-ups and registration walls or paywalls.
This differs from traffic coming via softer ad-blockers that still allow all or many of these monetisation options for publishers but hide the most aggressive advertising for users.
The report claims to have found 976 million users globally representing “dark traffic” across the web, totalling 18% of all web traffic. That’s up from 590 million in 2019.
It predicts that dark traffic will hit 1.1 billion users in 2026.
In the UK, the report found that 23% of web traffic is “dark”, representing 16 million users.
The report findings were based on a study of more than five billion “dark traffic” page views detected across Ad-Shield’s publisher network by its proprietary technology in 2024 and 2025, combined with a consumer survey of 2,616 respondents generating “dark” page views and some third-party data including previous industry estimates from 2019 to 2023, before Ad-Shield launched. Ad-Shield claims it can now detect and measure traffic that evades traditional ad-blocker detection tools.
The study discovered that the majority of users did not choose to block ads, with ad-blocking technology often activated by a third-party like their employer at a network level, their educational institution, security software they installed, or public Wi-Fi networks.
For example ad-blocking tech can be bundled with VPNs (virtual private networks that hide a web user’s location) and built into browsers like BRave and Duck Duck Go. There are also dedicated apps and cross-platform brands such as AdGuard which describes itself as “the world’s most advanced ad blocker” that can “even” block on Youtube.
Previously ad-blocking was mainly thought to be done through browser extensions added to the most-used browsers like Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox.
Under half (48%) of the survey respondents said they were fully aware they were ad-blocking, while 12% were somewhat aware and 40% were unaware.
Of those who block ads (including those who did not actively choose to), almost a quarter (23%) said they prefer not to see ads while 6% said they wanted to remove the most annoying ads and 6% did it for privacy reasons so they could not be tracked.
The report found that one type of advert proved the most irritating to users and most likely to trigger them to download an ad-blocked: pre-roll video adverts, which half (51%) said they find disruptive or frustrating.
The greatest proportion of users who self-activated a hard ad-blocker found out about it through advertising (34%), followed by word of mouth (31%) and media/social media (16%).
The report said: “These insights align with our ecosystem observations: many ad-block developers now market their products aggressively via Google Ads and programmatic placements, reaching users at scale.
“For publishers, this underlines the importance of awareness — brutal ad-blockers are no longer fringe tools. They’re mainstream products with real marketing budgets.”
The report was released on the same day that US trade association
News/Media Alliance announced it had secured the takedown of 12ft.io
, which helped people bypass paywalls and view websites without ads, trackers or pop-ups by disguising users’ browsers as a web crawler.
The trade body called it “illegal circumvention technology”, said 12ft.io has been locked by its web host, and promised to take similar action against other paywall bypassing technologies.
Paul Bannister, chief strategy officer at ad management company Raptive, described dark traffic as “one of those industry shifts that’s been happening quietly while we’ve all been focused elsewhere.
“What’s clear is the causes behind ad blocking have become fragmented. It’s no longer purely user driven. This requires a fresh and thoughtful approach. Given the scale of what this report presents, even solving parts of this puzzle could meaningfully impact publisher economics.”
Heather Carver, chief revenue officer at programmatic adtech company Freestar, said: “As an industry, we’ve known about ad-blocking for a long time. This report changes how we should think about it.
“The growth of dark traffic undermines the ability of publishers to fund the production of quality content, or even operate as a business. We must recognise users are not the main driver causing this.”

data.title: Texas ranks as No. 1 state with the most people in financial distress
data.author: paulpauper
data.article_summary: 根据WalletHub的最新研究，德克萨斯州在2025年成为全美财务困境最严重的州，尽管其经济规模较大且GDP较高。该研究通过比较50个州的九项指标，如平均信用评分、账户困境比例和破产申请变化等，得出这一结论。德州居民的平均信用评分在全国排第九低，破产申请量增加22%，且在贷款和债务相关的搜索指数中排名靠前，表明居民借贷需求迫切。除德州外，佛罗里达、路易斯安那、内华达和南卡罗来纳也位列财务困境最严重的前五州。而夏威夷、佛蒙特和阿拉斯加则是财务困境最少的州。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：德克萨斯州生活成本和经济因素

不同观点：
• RandomBacon认为德克萨斯州整体生活成本较低，但在四大城市中，生活成本较高。他指出以下几点：
  - 在这些大城市中，居民需要汽车来完成日常事务，这增加了财务负担。
  - 住房成本高。
  - 大量廉价劳动力压低了工资水平。
  - 这些因素可能导致德克萨斯州在某些生活成本指数中排名较高。

• chris_wot则关注德克萨斯州宽松的监管环境，认为这种环境可能是导致生活成本问题的一个重要因素。虽然没有详细展开，但暗示了监管政策对经济和生活成本的潜在影响。

补充讨论：
- RandomBacon的观点中提到了汽车拥有是财务负担的一个来源，这表明交通成本在德克萨斯州城市生活中是一个重要因素。
- chris_wot对监管环境的质疑引发了一个讨论点，即政策和法规如何影响生活成本和经济条件。
- 争议的焦点可能在于生活成本高的原因：是由于城市化带来的实际需求（如汽车拥有）还是由于政策和经济结构（如劳动力市场和监管环境）的影响。

这两个观点共同构成了对德克萨斯州生活成本问题的多角度分析，涉及到城市与农村的差异、交通需求、住房市场和政策环境等多个方面。
